statement: Overvalued no-bid award to a connected vendor — the $2.4M HVAC contract went to the official's neighbour at ~2.7× the budget line and ~2.2× the cheapest disqualified bid, with no emergency declaration on file.
evidenceFor: No-bid award of $2.4M against a $900k budget line
Vendor's registered address matches the awarding official's
Two cheaper bids disqualified on technicalities
Three independent records agree on the amount
evidenceAgainst: The contract recites 'emergency procurement' (no declaration produced)
A record-keeping error could explain the price gap
discriminatingTests: Is there an emergency declaration on file?

statement: Legitimate emergency procurement — the no-bid award was justified by an emergency declaration, so the price premium reflects urgency rather than favouritism.
evidenceFor: The contract text recites emergency procurement
evidenceAgainst: No emergency declaration has been produced in the FOIA drop
discriminatingTests: Is there an emergency declaration on file?

statement: Record-keeping error — the $2.4M figure or the award details are wrong, so there is no real overpayment to report.
evidenceFor: Municipal procurement records are notoriously inconsistent
evidenceAgainst: Three independent records agree on the amount
Budget line and two competitor bids corroborate the gap
discriminatingTests: Do independent records agree on the awarded amount?
